meta.profile: mid-maturity Australian bank (composite, fictional) — birthright provisioning and self-service request established, certification and SoD governance partially mature, role model and right-sizing still emerging
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic illustrative posture authored to demonstrate the reporting pipeline. Does not represent any real institution or assessment.

UC-I-001.rationale: Joiners receive birthright access automatically from the HR feed against versioned role policies, with the large majority of day-one access granted without manual tickets.

UC-I-002.rationale: Transfers add new-role birthright access but prior-role entitlements are rarely revoked, so privilege creep accumulates across role changes with no manager reaffirmation step.

UC-I-003.rationale: Leaver de-provisioning runs on a nightly batch from the HR source so the same-day disablement expectation (ASD ISM-0430) is not consistently met for contractors and federated SaaS targets.

UC-I-004.rationale: Account-to-owner reconciliation is performed only on a few critical systems; dormant accounts beyond the inactivity threshold are not systematically detected or disabled estate-wide.

UC-I-005.rationale: Annual certification campaigns run on schedule and most items are decisioned, but no-decision items currently default to retain rather than revoke and revocation actioning often slips past SLA.

UC-I-006.rationale: Privileged entitlements are flagged within the general campaign but lack a separate shorter cadence and a consistent named-owner sign-off, so the highest-impact access is not validated more often than ordinary access.

UC-I-007.rationale: There is no event-driven micro-certification; risk-relevant changes such as transfers or new privileged grants wait for the next scheduled campaign to be re-validated.

UC-I-008.rationale: Access requests are not evaluated against the SoD ruleset before provisioning, so toxic combinations are only discovered later during detective scans rather than blocked at the source.

UC-I-009.rationale: A versioned SoD ruleset with named owners exists for the SOX-relevant scope, but the violation-management workflow and time-bound exception re-attestation are only partly documented and applied.

UC-I-010.rationale: Detective SoD scans run on the SOX-critical ERP and core banking systems, but coverage of cross-system toxic pairs and a complete mitigating-control register across the wider estate is still incomplete.

UC-I-011.rationale: A formal role-mining and RBAC baseline exercise has not yet been scoped; entitlements are still largely granted individually and a coverage metric has not been captured.

UC-I-012.rationale: A self-service catalogue routes requests through an enforced manager-plus-owner approval chain with recorded approver, timestamp and justification, and most grants flow through the workflow rather than out-of-band.

UC-I-013.rationale: There is no periodic least-privilege right-sizing report driven by usage telemetry; standing excess access is added far more readily than it is removed, with no measured reduction trend.
